title: White Christmas
tagline: Snow's late in Vermont. Dinner isn't.
about: Two army mates turned song-and-dance stars put on a show to save their old general's struggling Vermont inn.
cue: Serve the snacks when the show at the Columbia Inn begins.
faces: No snow, no guests, but the General still gets a proper dinner. Keep the cocoa hot.

    StartersMidnight liverwurst on rye and buttermilkLiverwurst, mustard, pickles and red onion on rye, with cold buttermilkHow to make it8 slices of rye bread30g butter, soft1 tbsp wholegrain mustard250g liverwurst or smooth pork pate8 dill pickle slices1 red onion, in rings400ml well-chilled buttermilkSpread the bread with butter and a thin layer of mustard.Slice the liverwurst and lay it over half the slices. Top with pickles and red onion, then the other slices.Press down, trim the crusts and cut into fingers.Pour the buttermilk into small glasses and serve together.Columbia Inn cheese puffsLight choux puffs baked with sharp cheddarHow to make it100g butter150g plain flour4 eggs120g vintage cheddar, gratedBring water and the butter to the boil, beat in the flour until it forms a ball, then cool.Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the cheddar.Pipe small balls onto lined trays.Bake at 200°C until puffed and golden.Aged Vermont cheddar with apple butterSisters, sisters, never were there such.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsVermont inn roast turkeyRoast turkey breast with stuffing, cranberry sauce and roast potatoesHow to make it1.5kg turkey breast60g butter1 tbsp mixed dried herbs150g breadcrumbs1 onion, diced1 small bunch sage1kg potatoes, cut into chunks1 jar cranberry sauce3 tbsp olive oilRub the turkey with some of the butter and the herbs.Roast at 180°C.Mix the breadcrumbs with the onion, chopped sage and melted butter and bake the stuffing alongside the turkey.Toss the potatoes in oil and roast on another tray.Rest the turkey and serve with stuffing, cranberry sauce and potatoes.General Waverly's maple glazed hamFor the old General, the night the whole division turns upHow to make it2kg half leg ham1 tbsp whole cloves125ml maple syrup2 tbsp Dijon mustard1 orange2 tbsp brown sugarPeel the rind off the ham, leaving the fat, score it in diamonds and stud with cloves.Simmer the maple syrup with the mustard, sugar and juice of the orange until syrupy.Bake the ham at 180°C, brushing with glaze every 10 minutes, until sticky and dark.Rest, then carve thick.SweetsSnowy coconut cakeCoconut cake layers with cream cheese frosting rolled in coconutHow to make it200g butter, soft200g caster sugar4 eggs250g self-raising flour160g desiccated coconut150ml coconut milk250g cream cheese200g icing sugarBeat the butter with the sugar until pale, then add the eggs, flour, some of the coconut and the coconut milk.Bake in two tins at 175°C.Cool the cakes.Beat the cream cheese with the icing sugar, sandwich and cover the cakes.Roll the sides in the rest of the coconut.DrinksEggnog by the fireChilled egg custard drink with vanilla and nutmegHow to make it4 eggs (yolks only)100g caster sugar600ml full cream milk200ml thickened cream1 cinnamon stick1 tsp vanilla extract1 whole nutmegWhisk the yolks with the sugar.Heat the milk, cream, cinnamon stick and vanilla until steaming, whisk into the yolks and return to the pan.Stir over low heat until it coats a spoon.Chill.Serve with grated nutmeg.
